title: have to / don't have to
grammarTitle: have to / don't have to — obligation & choice
grammarNote: HAVE TO выражает ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНОСТЬ — то, что необходимо делать (внешняя необходимость, правила, требования). DON'T HAVE TO означает ОТСУТСТВИЕ ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬСТВА — ты можешь сделать, но не обязан. Важно: don't have to ≠ must not! 'Don't have to' = необязательно. 'Must not' = нельзя!

grammarTable.subject: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: I have to see a doctor. · You have to take this medicine.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She has to stay home. · He has to rest for three days.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: I don't have to go to hospital. · You don't have to take antibiotics.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She doesn't have to come in today. · He doesn't have to worry.

grammarTable.subject: Do you have to...?
grammarTable.example: Do you have to take medicine? · Does she have to rest?

grammarTable.subject: Short answers
grammarTable.example: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. · Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.

grammarTable.subject: Past: had to
grammarTable.example: I had to stay in bed for 3 days. · She had to see a specialist.

grammarTable.subject: Past negative
grammarTable.example: I didn't have to go to hospital. · He didn't have to take antibiotics.

rows.form: You have to drink 2 litres of water.
She has to stay home for 3 days.
Students have to attend lectures.
He has to take tablets twice a day.
I had to go to the clinic yesterday.
They had to wait 30 minutes.
You don't have to go to hospital.
rows.example: Not necessary — you can stay home.

rows.form: She doesn't have to take antibiotics.
I don't have to wake up early on Sunday.
He doesn't have to wear a suit.
rows.example: No dress code — choice is yours.

rows.form: They didn't have to pay.
You don't have to come — it's optional.

grammarExtra.title: ⚠️ don't have to vs must not (crucial difference!)

rows.form: You don't have to take aspirin.
rows.example: NOT obligatory — but you can if you want. ✅

rows.form: You must not take aspirin! (allergy!)
You don't have to come to the party.
rows.example: Optional — no pressure. You can come or not.

rows.form: You must not arrive late to the exam.
rows.example: Forbidden — it is against the rules.

rows.form: Do I have to take these tablets?
rows.example: Do I have to? — Yes, you do. Twice a day.

rows.form: Does she have to stay home?
rows.example: Does she have to? — Yes, she does. For 3 days.

rows.form: Do we have to bring anything?
rows.example: Do we have to? — No, you don't. Just yourself.

rows.form: Did you have to wait long?
rows.example: Did you have to wait? — Yes, I did. 30 minutes.

grammarTip:
Главное правило: have to = внешняя необходимость (правила, советы врача, законы)
must = внутренняя убеждённость (сам считаешь нужным)

ТРИ ключевых различия:
① have to (обязательно) → I have to take this medicine. Doctor said so.
② don't have to (необязательно) → I don't have to stay in bed. But I can if I want.
③ must not (запрещено!) → You must not drive after taking this medicine. Dangerous!

💡 don't have to ≠ must not — это РАЗНЫЕ значения!

exercises.text: Kamila ___ stay home for three days. (The doctor ordered it.)
exercises.hint: Doctor's order = obligation = has to (3rd person singular).

exercises.text: You ___ take antibiotics. (They are not necessary for this infection.)
Students ___ attend all lectures. (It is a university rule.)
"Don't have to" and "must not" have the same meaning.
exercises.hint: "Don't have to" = not necessary. "Must not" = forbidden. Very different!

exercises.text: ___ she have to see a specialist?
exercises.hint: She → Does she have to...? (3rd person singular)

exercises.text: Last week I was ill and I ___ stay in bed for two days.
exercises.hint: Past of have to → had to. (same for all persons)

exercises.text: ___ you have to take the tablets on an empty stomach?
Choose the sentence that means something is NOT ALLOWED.
opts: You don't have to eat before the test.
You must not eat before the test.
You don't have to wear a tie.
You don't have to come early.
exercises.correct: You must not eat before the test.

questions.text: She ___ rest for three days. (Doctor's instruction)
You ___ go to hospital — it's not that serious.
questions.hint: Not necessary (but possible) = don't have to.

questions.text: What is the difference between "don't have to" and "must not"?
opts: "don't have to" = not necessary; "must not" = forbidden
questions.correct: "don't have to" = not necessary; "must not" = forbidden
questions.hint: Critical difference: don't have to = optional. must not = prohibited.

questions.text: "I have to" and "I has to" are both correct.
questions.hint: I / You / We / They → have to. He/She/It → has to. Never "I has to".

questions.text: The past form of "have to" is ___
questions.hint: Past of have to = had to (all persons).

questions.text: ___ you have to take any medicine? — No, I ___ .
questions.hint: I/You → Do you have to? No, I don't.

opts: She had fun at the party.
She has to see a doctor today.
questions.correct: She has to see a doctor today.
questions.hint: has to = obligatory → She has to see a doctor.

opts: He doesn't have to take antibiotics.
questions.correct: He doesn't have to take antibiotics.

questions.text: "You must not drive" means it is not necessary to drive.
questions.hint: "must not" = FORBIDDEN. "don't have to" = not necessary. Very different!

questions.text: Last year, Kamila ___ take an exam twice because she was ill.
questions.hint: Past obligation: last year → had to.

questions.text: Does Amir have to stay in bed? — Yes, he ___ .
questions.hint: Short answer to Does...? → Yes, he does.

questions.text: At WKU, students ___ attend a minimum number of classes.
"She doesn't has to go" is correct.
questions.hint: She → doesn't have to (not 'doesn't has'). Always 'doesn't have to'.

questions.text: "You ___ smoke in the clinic." (It is forbidden!)
I ___ go to hospital last week — the doctor said it was serious.
Which sentence shows something is OPTIONAL (not required)?
opts: You have to take this medicine.
You must not eat before the test.
You don't have to bring a pen — we have extras.
questions.correct: You don't have to bring a pen — we have extras.
questions.hint: don't have to = not necessary, optional.
